newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: West Australia state seen growing six pct in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: West Australia state seen growing six pct in 97/98.

text.p: The Western Australian (WA) economy is forecast to grow by five per cent this year and by six percent in 1997/98 (July-June), state budget papers show.
The budget papers said the state's economy was forecast to grow by around five per cent over the period 1998/99 to 2000/01.
"The expansion of downstream processing activities is expected to underpin the substantial growth rates in the WA economy over the medium term," the budget paper said.
"This is also anticipated to strengthen the flow through of benefits from the resources sector to the broader economy through links to domestic manufacturing and service industries."
The treasury budget paper predicted business investment would rise by 10.75 percent in the current year and by 13 percent next year.
Consumer spending and dwelling activity were expected to rise in the second half of 1996/97 and grow at three percent and 8.25 percent respectively next year.

Public sector investment spending was forecast to rise 3.25 per cent in 1997/98, compared with 10 percent this year, but the budget paper said this would be largely offset by a moderation in public consumption spending associated with the fiscal consolidation within the Western Australian and Commonwealth general government sectors.
The state's industry structure was expected to further mature with the minerals and energy sector continuing to grow at a faster pace than other industries.
"Production capacity is set to increase substantially in the near term, with a number of projects currently under construction," the budget paper said.

"Significant expansions are anticipated in nickel, gold and iron ore, with production expected to commence in a number of projects before the end of 1998, including Anaconda Nickel's Murrin Murrin project," .
Growth in energy production was seen largely constrained by existing capacity, with the development of the Stag oil field the only major project expected to commence production in 1998.
Nevertheless, production from this field was expected to exceed production of the Wandoo "B" field.

"The outlook for manufacturing is highly favourable, with manufacturing set to account for an increasing proportion of state output. Growht is expected to be concentrated particularly in metal products manufacture.

"The gross value of agricultural production is forecast to decline by six per cent in 1997/98 to A$4 billion. The decline primarily reflects a fall in wheat and barley production from very strong levels in 1996/97. The price of most agricultural products is expected to remain relatively steady in 1997/97."
